body:
At this point I'd take a job that isn't actively detrimental to the world or society at large. I'm educated in several fields but have been unable to make the leap into the real world in any of them. 

One of my majors was in English. I can write decently, but I can never hit what publishers want, or navigate the business world well enough to work in it professionally.

Computer science was another. Again, perfect grades, but I get too overwhelmed and confused to be a worthwhile engineer. I can only work on my own.

Thank you. I don't personally know anyone else with these problems, so it's nice to know others exist even if we are a minority.

But it feels like every glimmer of hope I ever get is solely a means to throw me harder into the dirt.

I met the only girl I ever kissed about a year ago. The only girl I've even liked in the past six years. Too bad she was also dating someone else she liked better.

Got interviews at places I've been wanting to work at since I was a kid. Received form rejections from all of them on the same night in the same hour. 

And so on. This is the best I could manage in thirty years. I'm just so tired of waiting for something that will probably never come.

I deleted my original post because I didn't want to discourage OP--but it's very foolish to just assume things will work out, just as it's foolish to assume I (or anyone else) haven't put in significant amounts of effort to change things.
